deities: Goddess Mahalaxmi (main deity — black stone idol with four arms, goddess of wealth and prosperity)
Kuladevata family deities of the mahajan and upasak communities (the original 18th-century idol is preserved in a small box in the rear wall of the temple)

history.dynasty: Built by the Saraswat Brahmin community under Portuguese rule
history.period: Consecrated 10 July 1818 (Ashadh Shukla Saptami, Shaka 1739); completed 1819
history.summary: The Panaji Mahalaxmi temple descends from a pre-Portuguese shrine whose marble idol was hidden from the Portuguese: devotees carried it from Taleigao to Mayem village (Bicholim taluka) for safety, and in 1817 Narayan Kamat Mhamai of Panaji brought it back to Panjim after a dream of the deity. The present temple was built on land belonging to Purshottam Prabhu Sinari of Raibander with collected donations of 1006 sharafi, and the idol was consecrated on Friday, 10 July 1818 with approval from the Portuguese Governor-General (Conde-de-Rio-Pardo) under the Portuguese king's order — among the first Hindu temples permitted under Portuguese rule. Saraswat Brahmins are the mahajans; Sheth, Bhandari, Nhavi, Tarukar and Hindu Gaonkar communities of Bardez are also upasaks. The goddess is regarded as one of the ruling deities of Panjim. NOTE: a crowd-sourced site describes the temple as 'on Altinho hill'; the temple's official site and map data place it at Dr Dada Vaidya Road near Mushtifund in Panjim city centre — the Altinho claim is unverified.

name: Shree Mahalaxmi Temple
town_description: Panaji (Panjim) is the capital of Goa on the banks of the Mandovi river, known for its Portuguese-era Latin Quarter of Fontainhas, the Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception church, and the Adilshahi palace.

travel.airport: Dabolim (Goa International) Airport about 30 km; Manohar International Airport (Mopa) about 35 km.
travel.railway: Thivim station about 22 km; Karmali about 10 km.
travel.road: In central Panaji on Dr Dada Vaidya Road; well connected by local buses and taxis within the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (Goa's tourist season); Navaratri and Chaitra Purnima draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 6:00 AM to 8:30 PM daily (placeapp.in); the temple's own listing shows 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM — verify before visiting.
